1.why: All six screens show a static, uncluttered layout with no animations, carousels, or pop-ups.

2.why: Primary blue CTAs, bold headings, and the yellow Stay safe panel stand out clearly against the white forms.

3.why: Numbered step tabs, clear field labels, and a single prominent action button per screen make the needed control easy to locate.

4.why: The flow requires remembering or copying a recovery token, an MFA code, and complex password rules across five distinct steps.

5.why: No password-manager affordance, autofill attribute, or remember-me control appears on any screen.

6.why: The screens display only empty inputs and generic labels with no saved accounts, familiar devices, or previously entered values.

7.why: Instructional copy is mostly concise and readable, though a few paragraphs (Stay safe, privacy notice) run longer.

8.why: No error states or error messages are shown in any of the six screenshots, so the claim cannot be verified as true.

9.why: Password rules are stated in text but no example values, masked samples, or input placeholders illustrate what to type.

10.why: The UI offers no choice among password, code, face, or other login methods; only a fixed token-then-code-then-password sequence.

11.why: Each step presents essentially one primary button and at most one secondary link, avoiding choice overload.

12.why: The final Recovery complete screen states the outcome clearly, but intermediate verifications show no explicit success or failure feedback.

13.why: Persistent Stay safe tips, password-requirement text, and short instructional sentences appear on every step.

14.why: Fields can be re-filled and a Return to recovery start button exists on the last screen, yet no back buttons or explicit retry controls are visible on earlier steps.

15.why: Header, step indicator, card layout, Stay safe panel, Logs panel, and button styling remain identical across all six screens.
